title: Invalid request
meaning: The request is malformed: the JSON doesn't parse, a field is missing, unknown or of the wrong type, an amount has more than 2 decimal places, or a memo is over 150 characters. A misspelt field is an error, not an omitted one.
fix: Read `errors` in the response: it maps each bad field to its problems. Fix the request and send it again with a new timestamp.

title: Invalid signature
meaning: The TxG-Key-Id, TxG-Timestamp or TxG-Signature header is missing, or the signature doesn't match the request as TxGold received it.
fix: If you sign by hand, compare your canonical string with the one in `detail`: TxGold puts the string it verified there. The usual causes are signing a different body than the one sent (re-serializing the JSON after signing), changing the query string's encoding, or a proxy that rewrites the request. The SDKs sign exactly the bytes they send.

title: Timestamp out of range
meaning: TxG-Timestamp is too far from TxGold's clock: more than 3 minutes ahead, or more than 7 minutes behind.
fix: Check the server's clock (NTP). A retry of an old request can't be resent once it's out of the window: look the payment up instead, as in [Idempotency and retries](/guides/idempotency).

title: Key not found
meaning: TxGold doesn't know the key in TxG-Key-Id, or it belongs to the other environment (Sandbox and Production keys are separate).
fix: Check that you're using the key file for this environment, and that the key is still listed for the integration in the business portal.

title: Key expired
meaning: The key passed the expiry date set when it was added, or an Admin revoked it in the business portal.
fix: Add a new key to the integration in the business portal and switch to it. Add the new one before the old one expires to rotate without downtime.

title: Portal session not found
meaning: Returned to the business portal when the browser's key has no sign-in. Integrations never see it.
fix: Sign in to the portal again.

title: Portal session expired
meaning: Returned to the business portal when the sign-in has expired, was signed out, or was declined on the phone. Integrations never see it.
fix: Sign in to the portal again.

title: Sign-in not yet approved
meaning: Returned to the business portal while a sign-in waits for approval on the phone. Integrations never see it.
fix: Approve the sign-in in the TxGold app.

title: Forbidden
meaning: The key is valid but its role may not do this: a Device key sending a payment, a no-refunds role refunding, or a key acting on a TxGold system account.
fix: Use an integration with the Integration role for back-office work. An Admin can change an integration's role in the business portal.

title: Not found
meaning: The account, payment or payment request doesn't exist, or your key isn't attached to it. The two cases get the same answer on purpose, so ids can't be probed.
fix: Check the id, and that the key belongs to an integration on the account involved.

title: Duplicate request
meaning: The timestamp was already used for a different request from this account. Each TxG-Timestamp is also the request's idempotency key.
fix: Sign a new request with a new timestamp. To resend the same payment safely, resend the identical request: same timestamp and same body. See [Idempotency and retries](/guides/idempotency).

title: Already refunded
meaning: The payment already has a refund. A payment can be refunded once, in full or in part.
fix: Fetch the payment to see its `refundId` and `refundedAmount`. To return more, send a new payment to the customer.

title: Payment request is not pending
meaning: The payment request was already paid, dismissed, cancelled or has expired, so it can't be paid or cancelled. An open request stops being pending as soon as anyone pays it.
fix: Fetch the request to see its `status`. Create a new request if the customer still needs to pay.

title: Not pending
meaning: Returned to the business portal and the phone app when a sign-in or approval was already decided or has expired.
fix: Start the sign-in or change again.

title: Key already registered
meaning: Returned to the business portal when the public key being added is already in use.
fix: Generate a new key pair for each key you add.

title: Payload too large
meaning: The request body is over 64 KB. No API request needs more.
fix: Check that you're sending only the documented fields.

title: Insufficient balance
meaning: The paying account's balance doesn't cover the amount.
fix: Check the balance with `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}`. In the Sandbox, add test TxGold with the fund route.

title: Source and destination are the same account
meaning: The payment's source and destination are the same account.
fix: Check `destinationAccountId`.

title: Amount below minimum
meaning: Payments to a business or charity, and payment requests from one, must be more than 0.02 TxGold.
fix: Send a larger amount.

title: Source account inactive
meaning: The paying account isn't active.
fix: Contact TxGold support with the request id.

title: Identity check required
meaning: The account must finish its identity check in the TxGold app before it can do this, such as sending refunds.
fix: Complete the identity check in the TxGold app.

title: Destination account invalid
meaning: The account being paid doesn't exist or can't receive payments.
fix: Look the business up by its handle with `GET /v1/accounts/lookup` before paying it, and check the id.

title: Daily send limit exceeded
meaning: The payment would take the paying account over its daily sending limit.
fix: Try again tomorrow, or contact TxGold support about the account's limits.

title: Recipient balance limit exceeded
meaning: The payment would take the recipient over the balance their verification tier allows.
fix: Send a smaller amount. The recipient can raise their limit by completing more verification in the app.

title: Refund exceeds original payment
meaning: The refund amount is more than the payment received.
fix: Refund at most the payment's `amount`, or leave `amount` out to refund all of it.

title: Amount must match the payment request
meaning: A payment that names a `paymentRequestId` must be for exactly the requested amount.
fix: Use the request's `amount`.

title: Payment request cancelled or expired
meaning: The payment request was cancelled by the business, or passed its `expiresAt`.
fix: Ask the business for a new request.

title: Payer account invalid
meaning: The account asked to pay doesn't exist or can't be asked to pay, or no account has the `payerHandle` you gave.
fix: Check `payerAccountId`, or the handle: it must match an account's handle exactly (a leading @ is ignored).

title: Payer is not a sandbox demo customer
meaning: Sandbox only: `simulate pay` works only for requests sent to one of your business's demo customers, and for open requests paid by one.
fix: Create the request for one of the demo customers you were given with your Sandbox business. For an open request, name one of them as `payerAccountId`, or leave it out to use the first.

title: Business rule violation
meaning: A TxGold rule refused the request. `detail` says which.
fix: Read `detail`; contact TxGold support with the request id if it isn't clear.

title: Approval required
meaning: Returned to the business portal when a change, such as raising an integration's role, needs an Admin's approval on the phone.
fix: Ask for approval in the portal, then approve it in the TxGold app.

title: Internal error
meaning: Something failed on TxGold's side. No detail is given, by design.
fix: Retry later. For a payment, resend the identical request (same timestamp) so it can't be paid twice. Contact TxGold support with the request id if it keeps happening.

title: Rate unavailable
meaning: TxGold has no gold price to quote right now.
fix: Retry in a few minutes.

title: Sandbox unavailable
meaning: Sandbox only: the Sandbox can't create test TxGold at the moment.
fix: Retry later, or contact TxGold support.

title: Payment request already paid
meaning: Someone has already paid this open payment request. An open request (one made with no payer) can be paid once, by whoever pays first; a second payment is refused and nothing moves. Through the API a second attempt is normally refused earlier, with `request_not_pending`. This code is what a payment gets when it reaches the ledger anyway: two payers in the same instant, or a payer in the TxGold app.
fix: Fetch the request: it's `paid`, and `paymentId` is the payment that paid it. If this customer still owes you, create a new request for them.

title: Hold is not held
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

title: Hold expired
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

title: Hold is not open
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

title: Webhook endpoint disabled
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

title: Capture exceeds hold
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.

title: Widget limit reached
meaning: Returned to the business portal when a business that already has 50 pay widgets creates another. Deleted widgets don't count.
fix: Delete a widget you no longer use, then create the new one. See [Pay widget](/guides/pay-widget).

title: Recurring payment has ended
meaning: Not documented yet.
fix: Not documented yet.
